column1: # Live RBAC route matrix: Phase 6 (governance, RBAC_GOVERNANCE_ENABLED). Each step adds the rows of the behaviour it
# changes; a row of an earlier file whose answer a step changes is tagged superseded-by:p6 there.
# Columns: id, since, actor, method, path, body, expect, tags (see tests/rbac_matrix_live.sh).
# A governance:on row runs only while the webapp reads RBAC_GOVERNANCE_ENABLED on (it reads off while the permissions
# switch is off: flags.ts); a governance:off row only while it reads off. Off, every console route answers 404 before it
# reads the session or the database, so an admin's 404 there proves the route is absent, not refused. A request without a
# cookie never reaches a route (the middleware answers 401, in either state), so the anon rows carry no switch tag.
# Actors as seeded (webapp/scripts/e2e-rbac-seed.mjs): admin_a and admin_b are Full admins (no profile: no Root power,
# no admins:manage, no admin_profiles:manage, no instance:settings) and never Root; usermgr is the User manager
# (builtin:user-manager: users:* only); member_c holds no set (Default member). Every Root-only answer here is therefore
# 403 root_only, given before any password is checked; the confirmed Root's own writes run on the disposable instance
# (run_artifacts/combined_window/phase6_live.md section 8). "Allowed" is proved without a write: the request carries what
# the route refuses after its checks (a bad filter, a set id list that is not a list, a quota for an account that does not
# exist, a session id that cannot exist), so a refused caller still gets 401, 403 or 404. No row exports the audit log (an
# export writes an audit.exported row): its "allowed" rows send a format or a paging field the export refuses.
# ---- step 6.1: the console shell; /api/auth/me carries the switch every screen reads ----
# /admin and every page under it are Next's 404 with the switch off, decided in the server layout; on, the shell renders
# for any signed-in account (the sections it lists are decided in the browser from the same capabilities).
# ---- step 6.2: the users directory and one account's detail (users:read) ----
# The User manager reads both; a member and a Read-only analyst are refused naming users:read. The detail's Recent
# activity needs audit:read: the User manager gets the section's notice instead of rows.
# ---- step 6.3: the permission sets and admin profiles pages ----
# The pages sit under /admin; the APIs they call are Phase 3's and answer behind the permissions switch alone, whatever
# this one says (p3.tsv covers admin_a). The User manager lists the sets (users:assign_permissions: the directory's set
# filter and the Permissions dialog need them) but not the profiles; a Full admin is refused the profiles too.
# ---- step 6.4: projects and shares overviews (projects:oversee, users:read); Root's forced delete and revoke ----
# The shares list exists only while sharing is in force (404 otherwise, having read no share) and, with the default policy,
# lets admins see every share. Forced delete and force-revoke are the confirmed Root's: 403 root_only for a Full admin and
# for a member alike, before any password; the revoke checks sharing in force first (404 without it).
# ---- step 6.5: the operations view (platform:operations) and stopping one run ----
# A source that does not answer is named by its code and the view still answers 200. The stop asks platform:operations
# after the origin and the JSON body; a body that names no run is refused after it (400 invalid_target).
# ---- step 6.6: the audit viewer (audit:read), one row's details and the export (audit:export) ----
# ---- steps 6.6, 6.7, 6.8: the instance settings groups the switch adds ----
# With it on every administrator account reads the audit retention, which only the confirmed Root changes (403 root_only;
# a value under the floor is 400 first), and the instance:quotas holder (Full admin) reads and patches the quotas: a patch
# naming an account that does not exist is refused after the permission (400 unknown_quota_target, nothing written), the
# User manager is refused naming instance:quotas. With it off (identity on) neither group is shown or read from a body: the
# same PUTs change nothing and answer the settings. 36499 days is a valid value no fixture stores.
# ---- step 6.8: one account's quota and use ----
# My account reads its own, the admin detail another's under users:read (the User manager too); another member 403.
# ---- step 6.9: who may use a plugin (platform:plugins, the account read again) ----
# rbac-no-such-plugin is a valid id no plugin has: its rules read empty, with every member set a rule may name.
# The own list is the real signed-in account's; another account's takes users:revoke_sessions and the hierarchy (a Full
# admin or the User manager over a member; another admin only by the confirmed Root: 403 root_only); the own account is
# 400 own_account on the admin routes. rbac.no.such.session cannot be a session id, so a revoke ends after its checks
# ---- step 6.11: instance LLM providers; the agent's daily budget (internal key only) ----
# Root's routes are the confirmed Root's: 403 root_only for a Full admin and a member, before any password; the account's
# list is any signed-in account's (names and kinds only). With the switch off the budget answers unlimited and records
# nothing; on, it answers the person's limit and use. The scanner key and a browser session never reach the budget.
